definitions.explanation: A question or statement designed to be solved or guessed; a word game or brain teaser.
Something that is difficult to understand or explain; an unsolved question.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{謎|なぞ}{解|と}きを{楽|たの}しんだ。
{謎|なぞ}を{解|と}くのが{好|す}きだ。
examples.notes: 謎を解く = to solve a riddle/mystery

examples.japanese: この{謎|なぞ}{掛|か}けの{答|こた}えが{分|わ}かりますか。
examples.english: Can you figure out the answer to this riddle?

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}と{謎|なぞ}を{出|だ}し{合|あ}って{遊|あそ}んだ。
examples.english: I played with my friends, taking turns asking each other riddles.

examples.japanese: {謎|なぞ}の{人物|じんぶつ}が{現|あらわ}れた。
{宇宙|うちゅう}には{多|おお}くの{謎|なぞ}がある。
examples.english: There are many mysteries in the universe.

examples.japanese: この{事件|じけん}は{謎|なぞ}に{包|つつ}まれている。
examples.english: This case is shrouded in mystery.
examples.notes: 謎に包まれている = shrouded in mystery

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{行動|こうどう}は{謎|なぞ}だらけだ。
examples.english: His behavior is full of mysteries.

examples.japanese: {何年|なんねん}も{研究|けんきゅう}しても、この{謎|なぞ}は{解|と}けないままだ。
examples.english: Even after years of research, this mystery remains unsolved.

notes:
USAGE: {謎|なぞ} refers to both playful riddles and serious mysteries. Context determines which meaning applies.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{謎|なぞ}を{解|と}く (to solve a mystery/riddle)
・{謎|なぞ}が{解|と}ける (a mystery is solved)
・{謎|なぞ}に{包|つつ}まれる (to be shrouded in mystery)
・{謎|なぞ}が{深|ふか}まる (the mystery deepens)
・{謎|なぞ}{解|と}き (solving riddles; mystery-solving)

COMPOUNDS:
・{謎|なぞ}{掛|か}け (riddle, wordplay)
・{謎|なぞ}の{人物|じんぶつ} (mysterious person)
・{謎|なぞ}めいた (mysterious, enigmatic)

CULTURAL NOTE: {謎|なぞ}{掛|か}け is a traditional Japanese form of wordplay where the answer connects two seemingly unrelated things through a pun.
